sanskrit: kuvid aṅga namasā ye vṛdhāsaḥ purā devā anavadyāsa āsan | te vāyave manave bādhitāyāvāsayann uṣasaṁ sūryeṇa ||
english: Were there indeed those blameless gods of old who waxed great by homage? They, for Vāyu's sake and for distressed Manu, made the Dawn depart by means of the Sun.

sanskrit: uśantā dūtā na dabhāya gopā māsaś ca pāthaḥ śaradaś ca pūrvīḥ | indravāyū suṣṭutir vām iyānā mārḍīkam īṭṭe suvitaṁ ca navyam ||
english: Like willing messengers, like unwounding guardians, the months are your paths, and many autumns have been. O Indra-Vāyu, this hymn of praise comes to you seeking your grace and new well-being.

sanskrit: pīvoannāṁ rayivṛdhaḥ sumedhāḥ śvetaḥ siṣakti niyutām abhiśrīḥ | te vāyave samanaso vi tasthur viśven naraḥ svāpatyāni cakruḥ ||
english: The wise and radiant one, who increases wealth and whose lustre clings to rich food, accompanies the swift teams. For Vāyu's sake those men of one accord spread abroad, and performed all things for the welfare of their offspring.

sanskrit: yāvat taras tanvo yāvad ojo yāvan naraś cakṣasā dīdhyānāḥ | śuciṁ somaṁ śucipā pātam asme indravāyū sadatam barhir edam ||
english: So far as the vigour of the body, so far as the strength, so far as the men contemplating with vision — O pure drinkers Indra-Vāyu, drink the pure Soma pressed for us; be seated on this sacred grass.

sanskrit: niyuvānā niyutaḥ spārhavīrā indravāyū sarathaṁ yātam arvāk | idaṁ hi vām prabhṛtam madhvo agra adha prīṇānā vi mumuktam asme ||
english: Harnessing your desirable steeds, the swift teams, O Indra-Vāyu, come hither on one chariot. For this is the first portion of the mead offered to you; be satisfied and release your bounty upon us.

sanskrit: yā vāṁ śataṁ niyuto yāḥ sahasram indravāyū viśvavārāḥ sycante | ābhir yātaṁ suvidatrābhir arvāk pātaṁ narā pratibhṛtasya madhvaḥ ||
english: Whatever hundred, whatever thousand swift teams belonging to you, O Indra-Vāyu, all-desirable, attend you — with these most excellent ones come hither, O heroes, and drink of the mead that is offered.

sanskrit: arvanto na śravaso bhikṣamāṇā indravāyū suṣṭutibhir vasiṣṭhāḥ | vājayantaḥ sv avase huvema yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: We Vasiṣṭhas, like steeds craving renown, invoking Indra-Vāyu with well-wrought praises, seeking the contest, call you for protection. Do you always guard us with blessings.

sanskrit: ā vāyo bhūṣa śucipā upa naḥ sahasraṁ te niyuto viśvavāra | upo te andho madyam ayāmi yasya deva dadhiṣe pūrvapeyam ||
english: Come, Vāyu, O pure drinker, adorn yourself for us — your thousand swift teams are all-desirable. To you, O god, I bring the invigorating intoxicating drink of which you hold the right of first draught.

sanskrit: pra sotā jīro adhvareṣv asthāt somam indrāya vāyave pibadhyai | pra yad vām madhvo agriyam bharanty adhvaryavo devayantaḥ śacībhiḥ ||
english: The swift presser has stood forth at the sacrifices to press the Soma for Indra and Vāyu to drink. When the adhvaryus, devoted to the gods, bring forward with their acts the first portion of the mead for you two —

sanskrit: pra yābhir yāsi dāśvāṁsam acchā niyudbhir vāyav iṣṭaye duroṇe | ni no rayiṁ subhojasaṁ yuvasva ni vīraṁ gavyam aśvyaṁ ca rādhaḥ ||
english: With whatever swift teams you advance, O Vāyu, toward the worshipper for enjoyment in the house — yoke for us wealth rich in good food, yoke a hero, and cattle-wealth and horse-wealth as a gift.

sanskrit: ye vāyava indramādanāsa ādevāso nitośanāso aryaḥ | ghnanto vṛtrāṇi sūribhiḥ ṣyāma sāsahvāṁso yudhā nṛbhir amitrān ||
english: O Vāyu, those who bring joy to Indra, ungodlike, ever goading the noble foemen — smiting the obstructions together with generous patrons, may we, having overcome foes in battle with men, prevail.

sanskrit: ā no niyudbhiḥ śatinībhir adhvaraṁ sahasriṇībhir upa yāhi yajñam | vāyo asmin savane mādayasva yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: Come to our rite with your hundredfold swift teams, come to the sacrifice with your thousandfold. O Vāyu, rejoice at this pressing. Do you always guard us with blessings.

sanskrit: śuciṁ nu stomaṁ navajātam adyendrāgnī vṛtrahaṇā juṣethām | ubhā hi vāṁ suhavā johavīmi tā vājaṁ sadya uśate dheṣṭhā ||
english: May Indra-Agni, slayers of Vṛtra, take pleasure today in this pure, newly-born hymn. For I invoke you both with full voice — you who are easy to call; do you two, most eager to grant, immediately bestow the prize.

sanskrit: tā sānasī śavasānā hi bhūtaṁ sākaṁvṛdhā śavasā śūśuvāṁsā | kṣayantau rāyo yavasasya bhūreḥ pṛṅktaṁ vājasya sthavirasya ghṛṣveḥ ||
english: You two have truly been prosperous, jointly waxing in strength, growing together in might. Ruling over abundant wealth and rich pasture, mix for us the mighty, impetuous prize.

sanskrit: upo ha yad vidathaṁ vājino gur dhībhir viprāḥ pramatiṁ icchamānāḥ | arvanto na kāṣṭhāṁ nakṣamāṇā indrāgnī johuvato naras te ||
english: When the eloquent, wise men went to the assembly of the prize-winners, seeking guidance through their prayers — like steeds straining toward the goal, those men call upon Indra-Agni.

sanskrit: gīrbhir vipraḥ pramatiṁ icchamāna īṭṭe rayiṁ yaśasam pūrvabhājam | indrāgnī vṛtrahaṇā suvajrā pra no navyebhis tirataṁ deṣṇaiḥ ||
english: The sage, seeking guidance through his hymns, implores the glorious wealth that falls to the first share. O Indra-Agni, slayers of Vṛtra, wielders of the fine bolt, advance us further with new gifts.

sanskrit: saṁ yan mahī mithatī spardhamāne tanūrucā śūrasātā yataite | adevayuṁ vidathe devayubhiḥ satrā hataṁ somasutā janena ||
english: When the two great shining ones contend together, competing in the gain-of-heroes with self-radiant splendour — strike down the ungodly in the assembly together with the godly, as a body pressing the Soma.

sanskrit: imām u ṣu somasutim upa na endrāgnī saumanasāya yātam | nū cid dhi parimamnāthe asmān ā vāṁ śaśvadbhir vavṛtīya vājai̍ḥ ||
english: Come to us now at this Soma-pressing for our well-being, O Indra-Agni. For you have always paid attention to us; may I win you ever and again through the prizes.

sanskrit: so agna enā namasā samiddho 'cchā mitraṁ varuṇam indraṁ voceḥ | yat sīm āgaś cakṛmā tat su mṛḻa tad aryamāditiḥ śiśrathantu ||
english: O Agni, kindled with this oblation and homage, speak to Mitra, to Varuṇa, to Indra. Whatever sin we have committed — forgive that well; may Aryaman and Aditi loosen that bond.

sanskrit: etā agna āśuṣāṇāsa iṣṭīr yuvoḥ sacābhy aśyāma vājān | mendro no viṣṇur marutaḥ pari khyan yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: O Agni, through these swiftly performed rites, may we attain the prizes in concert with both of you. May Indra not pass us by, nor Viṣṇu, nor the Maruts. Do you always guard us with blessings.

sanskrit: iyaṁ vām asya manmana indrāgnī pūrvyastutiḥ | abhrād vṛṣṭir ivājani ||
english: This ancient praise-song to you two, O Indra-Agni, from this mind, has been born like rain from a cloud.

sanskrit: śṛṇutaṁ jaritor havam indrāgnī vanatam giraḥ | īśānā pipyataṁ dhiyaḥ ||
english: Hear the call of the singer, O Indra-Agni, take pleasure in the hymns. As lords, swell our prayers with your favour.

sanskrit: mā pāpatvāya no narendrāgnī mābhiśastaye | mā no rīradhatam nide ||
english: O Indra-Agni, do not deliver us, O heroes, to wickedness, nor to blame. Do not abandon us to reproach.

sanskrit: indre agnā namo bṛhat suvṛktim erayāmahe | dhiyā dhenā avasyavaḥ ||
english: We raise up the great homage and the well-fashioned praise to Indra and Agni, seeking help through prayer and song.

sanskrit: tā hi śaśvanta īḻata itthā viprāsa ūtaye | sabādho vājasātaye ||
english: For the eloquent men have ever thus invoked you two for help, in the press of battle, for the winning of the prize.

sanskrit: tā vāṁ gīrbhir vipanyavaḥ prayasvanto havāmahe | medhasātā saniṣyavaḥ ||
english: We who are eloquent, offering our libations, call upon you two with our hymns, seeking to win the sacrifice and the bounty.

sanskrit: indrāgnī avasā gatam asmabhyaṁ carṣaṇīsahā | mā no duḥśaṁsa īśata ||
english: Come to us with your protection, O Indra-Agni, overcomers of men. Let no evil-speaker have power over us.

sanskrit: mā kasya no araruṣo dhūrtiḥ pranaṅ martyasya | indrāgnī śarma yacchatam ||
english: Let no treachery of any hostile mortal injure us. O Indra-Agni, bestow shelter upon us.

sanskrit: gomad dhiraṇyavad vasu yad vām aśvāvad īmahe | indrāgnī tad vanemahi ||
english: The wealth rich in cattle, rich in gold, rich in horses — that which we implore of you two, O Indra-Agni, may we win that.

sanskrit: yat soma ā sute nara indrāgnī ajohavuḥ | saptīvantā saparyavaḥ ||
english: When the men who worship with horses call on Indra-Agni at the pressing of the Soma —

sanskrit: ukthebhir vṛtrahantamā yā mandānā cid ā girā | āṅgūṣair āvivāsataḥ ||
english: Those two who are greatest slayers of Vṛtra — they, rejoiced even by the hymn, are worshipped with praises and with lauds.

sanskrit: tāv id duḥśaṁsaṁ martyaṁ durvidvāṁsaṁ rakṣasvinam | ābhogaṁ hanmanā hatam udadhiṁ hanmanā hatam ||
english: Those two — let them strike down with their weapon the evil-speaking, ill-knowing, demon-possessed mortal; the greedy one — strike him down with your weapon; the flood-like one — strike him down with your weapon.

sanskrit: pra kṣodasā dhāyasā sasra eṣā sarasvatī dharuṇam āyasī pūḥ | prabābadhānā rathyeva yāti viśvā apo mahinā sindhur anyāḥ ||
english: This Sarasvatī, the iron-built fortress, surges forward with her flood and nurturing stream. Pressing onwards like a charioteer she goes, surpassing in greatness all other rivers and streams.

sanskrit: ekāceta sarasvatī nadīnāṁ śucir yatī giribhya ā samudrāt | rāyaś cetantī bhuvanasya bhūreḥ ghṛtam payo duduhe nāhuṣāya ||
english: Sarasvatī alone has perceived among rivers — pure, flowing from the mountains to the sea; perceiving the wealth of the abundant world, she has yielded milk and ghee for Nahuṣa.

sanskrit: sa vāvṛdhe naryo yoṣaṇāsu vṛṣā śiśur vṛṣabho yajñiyāsu | sa vājinam maghavadbhyo dadhāti vi sātaye tanvaṁ māmṛjīta ||
english: She has grown mightily among the women, a bull-calf, a bull among the sacred females. She bestows the prize-winning horse upon the generous patrons, and spreads herself wide for the winning.

sanskrit: uta syā naḥ sarasvatī juṣāṇopā śravat subhagā yajñe asmin | mitajñubhir namasyair iyānā rāyā yujā cid uttarā sakhib̈hyaḥ ||
english: And may that fair Sarasvatī, well-pleased, hearken to us at this sacrifice; coming with those who reverently bow their knees in homage, may she, even with wealth as her companion, be supreme among friends.

sanskrit: imā juhvānā yuṣmad ā namobhiḥ prati stomam sarasvati juṣasva | tava śarman priyatame dadhānā upa stheyāma śaraṇaṁ na vṛkṣam ||
english: O Sarasvatī, as we pour oblations to you, be pleased with this hymn of praise offered from our homage. May we, established in your most beloved shelter, stand under you as under the shelter of a tree.

sanskrit: ayam u te sarasvati vasiṣṭho dvārāv ṛtasya subhage vy āvaḥ | vardha śubhre stuvate rāsi vājān yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: O Sarasvatī, this Vasiṣṭha has thrown open for you the two doors of Ṛta, O beautiful one. Increase the one who praises you; grant him prizes, O bright goddess. Do you always guard us with blessings.

sanskrit: bṛhad u gāyiṣe vaco 'suryā nadīnām | sarasvatīm in mahayā suvṛktibhiḥ stomair vasiṣṭha rodasī ||
english: I shall sing a great word of lordly power — O Vasiṣṭha, magnify Sarasvatī alone with well-wrought praises, with hymns to both worlds.

sanskrit: ubhe yat te mahinā śubhre andhasī adhikṣiyanti pūravaḥ | sā no bodhy avitrī marutsakhā coda rādho maghonām ||
english: Since the Pūrus dwell in your two bright, mighty floods, O Sarasvatī — be our protectress, allied with the Maruts, and urge forward the bounty of the generous ones.

sanskrit: bhadram id bhadrā kṛṇavat sarasvaty akavārī cetati vājinīvatī | gṛṇānā jamadagnivat stuvānā ca vasiṣṭhavat ||
english: The auspicious Sarasvatī, wholly free from flaw, the prize-bearing, shall bring about what is auspicious. Being praised as Jamadagni praises, and lauded as Vasiṣṭha lauds.

sanskrit: janīyanto nv agravaḥ putrīyantaḥ sudānavaḥ | sarasvantaṁ havāmahe ||
english: Seeking wives, O first-born ones, seeking sons, O liberal givers — we invoke Sarasvat.

sanskrit: ye te sarasva ūrmayo madhuvanto ghṛtaścutaḥ | tebhir no 'vitā bhava ||
english: O Sarasvat, your waves that are sweet as honey and dripping with ghee — with these become our protector.

sanskrit: pīpivāṁsaṁ sarasvataḥ stanaṁ yo viśvadarśataḥ | bhakṣīmahi prajām iṣam ||
english: May we partake of the swollen breast of Sarasvat who is visible to all, receiving offspring and nourishment.

sanskrit: yajñe divo nṛṣadane pṛthivyā naro yatra devayavo madanti | indrāya yatra savanāni sunve gamat madāya prathamaṁ vayaś ca ||
english: At the sacrifice, in the seat of men of heaven and earth, where the godly men rejoice — where the Soma-pressings are pressed for Indra, and the first nourishment and delight come —

sanskrit: ā daivyā vṛṇīmahe 'vāṁsi bṛhaspatirnō maha ā sakhāyaḥ | yathā bhavema mīḻhuṣe anāgā yo no dātā parāvataḥ piteva ||
english: We choose the divine aids; may Bṛhaspati be our great ally and friend, that we may stand blameless before the bountiful one who gives to us from afar like a father.

sanskrit: tam u jyeṣṭhaṁ namasā havirbhiḥ suśevam brahmaṇas patiṁ gṛṇīṣe | indraṁ śloko mahi daivyaḥ siṣaktu yo brahmaṇo devakṛtasya rājā ||
english: Him, the eldest, the most pleasant lord of prayer, I praise with homage and oblations. May the great divine praise cleave to Indra, who is the king of the prayer that is god-made.

sanskrit: sa ā no yoniṁ sadatu preṣṭho bṛhaspatiṛ viśvavāro yo asti | kāmo rāyaḥ suvīryasya taṁ dāt parṣan no ati saścato ariṣṭān ||
english: May Bṛhaspati, who is all-desirable and most dear, take his seat in our place. May he grant the desire of wealth with heroic offspring, and lead us safely past all unbroken dangers.

sanskrit: tam ā no arkam amṛtāya juṣṭam ime dhāsur amṛtāsaḥ purājāḥ | śucikrandaṁ yajatam pastyānām bṛhaspatiṁ anarvāṇaṁ huvema ||
english: These immortals, ancient-born, have set up that song of praise dear to the immortal. We invoke Bṛhaspati, the pure-voiced, worthy of worship, lord of households, unwounded.

sanskrit: taṁ śagmāso aruṣāso aśvā bṛhaspatiṁ sahavāho vahanti | sahaś cid yasya nīlavat sadasthaṁ nabho na rūpam aruṣaṁ vasānāḥ ||
english: Vigorous, ruddy horses carry Bṛhaspati, drawing together. His assembly-place too, clothed in a form red as the sun, is deep-dark in its strength, like a cloud.

sanskrit: sa hi śuciḥ śatapatraḥ sa śundhyur hiraṇyavāśīr iṣiraḥ svarsāḥ | bṛhaspatiḥ sa svāveśa ṛṣvaḥ purū sakhib̈hya āsutim kariṣṭhaḥ ||
english: He is pure, hundred-winged, cleansing, swift with a golden axe, winning the light. Bṛhaspati of good appearance, noble, is most capable of bringing the libation to many friends.

sanskrit: devī devasya rodasī janitrī bṛhaspatiṁ vāvṛdhatur mahitvā | dakṣāyyāya dakṣatā sakhāyaḥ karad brahmaṇe sutarā sugādhā ||
english: The two divine worlds, heaven and earth, mothers of the god, have increased Bṛhaspati by their greatness. May the power of friends, fit for mastery, make the prayer easy to ford and easy to sound for the lord of prayer.

sanskrit: iyaṁ vām brahmaṇas pate suvṛktir brahmendrāya vajriṇe akāri | aviṣṭaṁ dhiyo jigṛtam puramdhīr jajastam aryo vanuṣām arātīḥ ||
english: O Lord of Prayer, this well-wrought prayer-hymn has been fashioned for you and for bolt-wielding Indra. Strengthen our thoughts, seize the full minds, consume the noble man's hostile treasures.

sanskrit: bṛhaspate yuvam indraś ca vasvo divyasyeśāthe uta pārthivasya | dhattaṁ rayiṁ stuvate kīraye cid yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: O Bṛhaspati, you and Indra are lords of heavenly and earthly wealth. Bestow riches on the one who praises, even on the one who sings your glory. Do you always guard us with blessings.

sanskrit: adhvaryavo aruṇaṁ dugdham aṁśuṁ juhota na vṛṣabhāya kṣitīnām | gaurād vedīyāṁ avapānam indro viśvāhed yāti sutasomam icchan ||
english: O Adhvaryus, offer the red-pressed, milked stalk to the bull of the peoples. Indra comes nearer than the wild ox to the drinking-place, ever going and seeking the pressed Soma.

sanskrit: yad dadhiṣe pradivi cārv annaṁ dive-dive pītim id asya vakṣi | uta hṛdota manasā juṣāṇa uśann indra prasthitān pāhi somān ||
english: Whatever fair food you have accepted from of old, day by day you carry off his draught. O Indra, enjoying it with heart and mind, and longing, protect the Soma-draughts set forth.

sanskrit: jajñānaḥ somaṁ sahase papātha pra te mātā mahimānam uvāca | endra papratho urv antariksaṁ yudhā devebhyo varivaś cakartha ||
english: At your very birth you drank the Soma for strength; your mother has proclaimed your greatness. O Indra, you spread out the wide atmosphere, and in battle you made room for the gods.

sanskrit: yad yodhayā mahato manyamānān sākṣāma tān bāhubhiḥ śāśadānāḥ | yad vā nṛbhir vṛta indrābhiyudhyās taṁ tvayājiṁ sauśravasaṁ jayema ||
english: When you made those who deemed themselves great fight each other, and we overcame them with our arms repeatedly — when you, O Indra, surrounded by heroes, fight against them — may we win through you that battle of good fame.

sanskrit: prendra̍sya vocam prathamā kṛtāni pra nūtanā maghavā yā cakāra | yad edadevīr asahiṣṭa māyā athābhavat kevalaḥ somo asya ||
english: I will proclaim the former deeds of Indra, and the new ones that the bountiful one has performed. When he overcame the ungodly magical powers, then the Soma became his alone.

sanskrit: tavedam viśvam abhitaḥ paśavyaṁ yat paśyasi cakṣasā sūryasya | gavām asi gopatiṛ eka indra bhakṣīmahi te prayatasya vasvaḥ ||
english: All this world around you that is rich in cattle — all that you see with the eye of the Sun — you alone are the master of the cows, O Indra. May we partake of your offered wealth.

sanskrit: bṛhaspate yuvam indraś ca vasvo divyasyeśāthe uta pārthivasya | dhattaṁ rayiṁ stuvate kīraye cid yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: O Bṛhaspati, you and Indra are lords of heavenly and earthly wealth. Bestow riches on the one who praises, even on the one who sings your glory. Do you always guard us with blessings.

sanskrit: paro mātrāyā tanvā vṛdhāna na te mahitvam anv aśnuvanti | ubhe te vidma rajas pṛthivyā viṣṇo deva tvam paramasya vitse ||
english: Growing beyond measure with your body, none attain to your greatness. We know your two realms of space and of earth, O Viṣṇu, god — you know the highest.

sanskrit: na te viṣṇo jāyamāno na jāto deva mahimnaḥ param antam āpa | ud astabhnā nākam ṛṣvaṁ bṛhantaṁ dādharta prācīṁ kakubham pṛthivyāḥ ||
english: Neither one being born nor one already born, O Viṣṇu, god, has attained the farthest limit of your greatness. You have propped up the lofty, vast vault of heaven, and you have established the eastern direction of the earth.

sanskrit: irāvatī dhenumatī hi bhūtaṁ sūyavasinī manuṣe daśasyā | vy astabhnā rodasī viṣṇav ete dādharta pṛthivīm abhito mayūkhaiḥ ||
english: You two have truly been rich in nourishment and cattle, rich in good pasture, conferring gifts upon Manu. O Viṣṇu, you have propped apart these two worlds, you have established the earth on all sides with your pillars.

sanskrit: uruṁ yajñāya cakrathur u lokaṁ janayantā sūryam uṣāsam agnim | dāsasya cid vṛṣaśiprasya māyā jaghnathur narā pṛtanājyeṣu ||
english: You two made wide room for sacrifice, giving birth to the Sun, to Dawn, to Fire. O heroes, you smashed the sorceries of the Dāsa Vṛṣaśipra in the battles.

sanskrit: indrāviṣṇū dṛṁhitāḥ śambarasya nava puro navatim ca śnathiṣṭam | śataṁ varcinas sahasraṁ ca sākaṁ hato apratya̍surasya vīrān ||
english: O Indra-Viṣṇu, you smashed the ninety-nine fortresses of Śambara. Together you slew a hundred and a thousand warriors of the irresistible Asura.

sanskrit: iyam manīṣā bṛhatī bṛhanto rukramā tavasā vardhayanitī | rare vāṁ stomaṁ vidatheṣu viṣṇo pinvatam iṣo vṛjaneṣu indra ||
english: This great wisdom, growing great with power, with wide strides — I have offered you this hymn at assemblies, O Viṣṇu. O Indra, swell our refreshments in the communities.

sanskrit: vaṣaṭ te viṣṇav āsa ā kṛṇomi tan me juṣasva śipiviṣṭa havyam | vardhantu tvā suṣṭutayo giro me yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: O Viṣṇu, I make the vaṣaṭ-call to your mouth — O Śipiviṣṭa, take pleasure in my oblation. May my praises and my hymns increase you. Do you always guard us with blessings.

sanskrit: nū marto dayate saniṣyan yo viṣṇava urugāyāya dāśat | pra yaḥ satrācā manasā yajāta etāvantaṁ naryam āvivāsāt ||
english: Now the mortal who worships and wishes to gain — who has offered to Viṣṇu of the wide stride — he who with a wholehearted mind has worshipped and sought to please this manly one —

sanskrit: tvaṁ viṣṇo sumatiṁ viśvajanyām aprayutām evayāvo matiṁ dāḥ | parco yathā naḥ suvitasya bhūrer aśvāvataḥ puruścandrasya rāyaḥ ||
english: O Viṣṇu of swift course, grant us a goodwill that is universal, never-failing, and a prayer — so that we may have the abundant well-being, the horse-rich and greatly-glorious wealth.

sanskrit: trir devaḥ pṛthivīm eṣa etāṁ vi cakrame śatarcasam mahitvā | pra viṣṇur astu tavasas tavīyān teṣaṁ hy asya sthavirasya nāma ||
english: Three times has this god strode across this earth of a hundredfold abundance by his greatness. Let Viṣṇu be mightier than the mighty; for the name of this ancient one is terrible.

sanskrit: vi cakrame pṛthivīm eṣa etāṁ kṣetrāya viṣṇuṛ manuṣe daśasyan | dhruvāso asya kīrayo janāsa urukṣitiṁ sujanimā cakāra ||
english: This Viṣṇu strode across this earth to grant it as a field to Manu. His peoples stand firm and immoveable; he of noble birth has made a broad dwelling.

sanskrit: pra tat te adya śipiviṣṭa nāmāryaḥ śaṁsāmi vayu̍nāni vidvān | taṁ tvā gṛṇāmi tavasam atatvyān kṣayantam asya rajasaḥ parāke ||
english: This your name, O Śipiviṣṭa — your noble name — I, knowing your manifestations, proclaim today. I praise you who are mighty, stronger than the strong, ruling over this realm in the far distance.

sanskrit: kim it te viṣṇo paricakṣyam bhūt pra yad vakṣe śipiviṣṭo asmi | mā varpo asmad apa gūha etad yad anyarūpaḥ samithe babhūtha ||
english: What, O Viṣṇu, should be concealed by you, when you declare, 'I am Śipiviṣṭa'? Do not hide this form from us — that form in which you appeared of altered shape in the battle.

sanskrit: vaṣaṭ te viṣṇav āsa ā kṛṇomi tan me juṣasva śipiviṣṭa havyam | vardhantu tvā suṣṭutayo giro me yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: O Viṣṇu, I make the vaṣaṭ-call to your mouth — O Śipiviṣṭa, take pleasure in my oblation. May my praises and my hymns increase you. Do you always guard us with blessings.

sanskrit: tisro vācaḥ pra vada jyotiragrā yā etad duhre madhudogham ūdhaḥ | sa vatsaṁ kṛṇvan garbham oṣadhīnāṁ sadyo jāto vṛṣabho roravīti ||
english: Speak forth the three voices, light-tipped, those that milk this sweet-milking udder — he who makes the calf, the germ of plants, roars aloud as a bull, born at once.

sanskrit: yo vardhan oṣadhīnāṁ yo apāṁ yo viśvasya jagato deva īśe | sa tridhātu śaraṇaṁ śarma yaṁsat trivartujyotiḥ svabhiṣṭy asme ||
english: He who nourishes the plants, who rules the waters, who is lord of all that moves, O god — may he grant us threefold shelter and comfort, and the three-turning light for our own satisfaction.

sanskrit: starīr u tvad bhavati sūta u tvad yathāvaśaṁ tanvaṁ cakra eṣaḥ | pituḥ payaḥ prati gṛbhṇāti mātā tena pitā vardhate tena putraḥ ||
english: From you the barren becomes fruitful, and from you the fertile one — this one has shaped the body as he willed. The mother receives the father's milk; by that the father grows, by that the son grows.

sanskrit: yasmin viśvāni bhuvanāni tastus tisro dyāvas tredhā sasrur āpaḥ | trayaḥ kośāsa upasecanāso madhvaḥ ścotanty abhito virapśam ||
english: In him all beings stand; the three heavens have flowed in three ways, and the waters flow — three vessels, ladle-like, drip the honey-mead around the mighty one.

sanskrit: idaṁ vacaḥ parjanyāya svarāje hṛdo astv antaram taj jujoṣat | mayobhuvo vṛṣṭayaḥ santv asme supippalā oṣadhīr devagopāḥ ||
english: May this word be inmost in the heart of Parjanya the self-ruler, may he take joy in it. May the rains bring well-being upon us; may the herbs be well-beaded and god-protected.

sanskrit: sa retodhā vṛṣabhaḥ śaśvatīnāṁ tasminn ātmā jagatas tasthusaś ca | tan ma ṛtam pātu śataśāradāya yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: He is the seed-sower, the bull of all the eternal ones; in him rests the Self of the moving and the standing. May that Ṛta protect me for a hundred autumns. Do you always guard us with blessings.

sanskrit: parjanyāya pra gāyata divas putrāya mīḻhuṣe | sa no yavasam icchatu ||
english: Sing forth to Parjanya, son of heaven, the bountiful. May he seek out pasture for us.

sanskrit: yo garbham oṣadhīnāṁ gavāṁ kṛṇoty arvatām | parjanyaḥ puruṣīṇām ||
english: Parjanya — who makes the germ of the plants, of the cows, of the mares, of women.

sanskrit: tasmā id āsye havir juhota madhvattamam | iḷāṁ naḥ saṁyataṁ karat ||
english: To him — pour into his mouth the most honey-sweet oblation. May he bring us the combined refreshment of Iḷā.

sanskrit: saṁvatsaraṁ śaśayānā brāhmaṇā vratacāriṇaḥ | vācam parjanyajinvitāṁ pra maṇḍūkā avādiṣuḥ ||
english: Lying still for a year like Brāhmaṇas observing their vow, the frogs have raised their voice set in motion by Parjanya.

sanskrit: divyā āpo abhi yad enam āyan dṛtiṁ na śuṣkaṁ sarasī śayānam | gavām aha na māyur vatsinīnām maṇḍūkānāṁ vaghur atra sam eti ||
english: When the heavenly waters came over him — like a dry bladder lying in a pool — the voice of the frogs, like the lowing of cattle and the lowing of cows with calves, comes together here.

sanskrit: yad īm enāṁ uśato abhy avarasīt tṛṣyāvataḥ prāvṛṣy āgatāyām | akhkhalīkṛtyā pitaraṁ na putro anyo anyam upa vadantam eti ||
english: When the rains came down upon them as they were longing and thirsty at the coming of the rainy season, one approaches the other who is speaking, as a son approaches his father, making the akhkhalī sound.

sanskrit: anyo anyam anu gṛbhṇāty enor apāṁ prasarge yad amandiṣātām | maṇḍūko yad abhivṛṣṭaḥ kaniṣkan pṛśniḥ saṁpṛṅkte haritena vācam ||
english: One grasps the other of the two when, rejoicing at the flowing of the waters — when the frog rained upon leaps about, the spotted one mingles its voice with the green one.

sanskrit: yad eṣām anyo anyasya vācaṁ śāktasyeva vadati śikṣamāṇaḥ | sarvaṁ tad eṣāṁ samṛdheva parva yat suvāco vadathanādhy apsu ||
english: When one of them speaks the voice of the other like a pupil practising — everything of them, when you speak well on the waters, is like a season of their prosperity.

sanskrit: gomāyur eko ajamāyur ekaḥ pṛśnir eko harita eka eṣām | samānaṁ nāma bibhrato virūpāḥ purūtrā vācam pipiśur vadantaḥ ||
english: One of them is cow-lowing, one is goat-lowing, one is spotted, and one is green. Bearing the same name though different in form, they have patterned their voice in many ways as they speak.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāso atirātre na some saro na pūrṇam abhito vadantaḥ | saṁvatsarasya tad ahaḥ pari ṣṭha yan maṇḍūkāḥ prāvṛṣīṇam babhūva ||
english: Like Brāhmaṇas at the all-night Soma-feast, speaking all around like a full lake — that day of the year has come round on which the frogs have entered the rainy season.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāsaḥ somino vācam akrata brahma kṛṇvantaḥ parivatsar āṇam | adhvaryavo gharmiṇaḥ siṣvidānā āvir bhavanti guhyā na ke cit ||
english: The Brāhmaṇas, Soma-drinkers, have raised their voice, performing the annual prayer. The sweating adhvaryus heating the cauldron appear — as if none are hidden.

sanskrit: devahitiṁ jugupur dvādaśasya ṛtuṁ naro na pra minanty ete | saṁvatsare prāvṛṣy āgatāyāṁ taptā gharmā aśnuvate visargam ||
english: They have guarded the divine ordinance of the twelve months; these men do not transgress the season. At the coming of the rainy season in the year, the heated caldrons obtain their discharge.

sanskrit: gomāyur adād ajamāyur adāt pṛśnir adād harito no vasūni | gavāṁ maṇḍūkā dadataḥ śatāni sahasrasāve pra tiranta āyuḥ ||
english: The cow-lowing one has given, the goat-lowing one has given, the spotted one has given, the green one has given us goods. The frogs who give hundreds of cows extend their life at the thousandfold pressing.

sanskrit: indrāsomā tapataṁ rakṣa ubjataṁ ny arpayataṁ vṛṣaṇā tamovṛdhaḥ | parā śṛṇītam acito ny oṣataṁ hataṁ nudethāṁ ni śiśītam atriṇaḥ ||
english: O Indra-Soma, scorch the demon, crush it, hurl down those that increase darkness, O mighty ones. Cast them away from us, burn them up — strike them, drive away, and utterly destroy the devourers.

sanskrit: indrāsomā sam aghaśaṁsam abhy aghaṁ tapur yayastu carur agnivām̐ iva | brahmadviṣe kravyāde ghoracakṣase dveṣo dhattam anavāyaṁ kimīdine ||
english: O Indra-Soma, let a heated cooking-pot of fire pursue the evil-speaker, the sinful one. Place an inescapable hatred upon the hater of prayer, the flesh-eater, the one of terrible glance, the kimīdin.

sanskrit: indrāsomā duṣkṛto vavre antar anārambhaṇe tamasi pra vidhyatam | yathā nātaḥ punar ekaś ca nodayat tad vām astu sahase manyumac chavaḥ ||
english: O Indra-Soma, pierce the evil-doers into the cave, into the darkness which has no foothold. May not one of them emerge from there again — let that wrathful strength of yours accomplish this.

sanskrit: indrāsomā vartayataṁ divo vadhaṁ sam pṛthivyā aghaśaṁsāya tarhaṇam | ut takṣataṁ svaryam parvatebhyo yena rakṣo vāvṛdhānaṁ nijūrvataḥ ||
english: O Indra-Soma, hurl down the weapon from heaven, the crusher from the earth upon the evil-speaker. Hew out the solar bolt from the mountains with which you smite the demon that has waxed great.

sanskrit: indrāsomā vartayataṁ divas pary agnitaptebhir yuvam aśmahanmabhiḥ | tapurvadhebhir ajarebhir atriṇo ni parśāne vidhyataṁ yantu nisvaram ||
english: O Indra-Soma, hurl from heaven with your fire-heated stone-smiting weapons, with your burning, ageless weapons, pierce the devourers in the ribs — let them go to silence.

sanskrit: indrāsomā pari vām bhūtu viśvata iyam matiḥ kakṣyāśveva vājinā | yāṁ vāṁ hotrām pari hinomi medhayemā brahmāṇi nṛpatīva jinvatam ||
english: O Indra-Soma, may this thought encompass you on all sides, like a girth around a prize horse. With this oblation I send forth to you both — quicken these prayers as a king of men.

sanskrit: prati smarethāṁ tujyadbhir evair hataṁ druho rakṣaso bhaṅgurāvataḥ | indrāsomā duṣkṛte mā sugam bhūd yo naḥ kadā cid abhidāsati druhā ||
english: Remember with your smiting courses — slay the deceitful demon, the destroyer. O Indra-Soma, let there be no easy path for the evil-doer who at any time would harm us treacherously.

sanskrit: yo mā pākena manasā carantam abhicaṣṭe anṛtebhir vacobhiḥ | āpa iva kāśinā saṁgṛbhītā asann astv āsata indra vaktā ||
english: He who assails me as I go with a simple mind, attacking me with false words — like waters clasped by a shining sieve, let his speech be empty, O Indra, let him who sits there be a speaker of nothing.

sanskrit: ye pākaśaṁsaṁ viharanta evair ye vā bhadraṁ dūṣayanti svadhābhiḥ | ahaye vā tān pradadātu soma ā vā dadhātu nirṛter upasthe ||
english: Those who scatter the praise of the simple man with tricks, and those who corrupt the good with their crooked ways — may Soma deliver them to the serpent, or place them in the lap of Nirṛti.

sanskrit: yo no rasaṁ dipsati pitvo agne yo aśvānāṁ yo gavāṁ yas tanūnām | ripuḥ stenaḥ steyakṛd dabhram etu ni ṣa hīyatāṁ tanvā tanā ca ||
english: O Agni, whoever would injure the taste of our food, or of our horses, of our cattle, of our bodies — the traitor, the thief, the one who commits theft, a little let him come — let him be abandoned with body and descendants.

sanskrit: paraḥ so astu tanvā tanā ca tisraḥ pṛthivīr adho astu viśvāḥ | prati śuṣyatu yaśo asya devā yo no divā dipsati yaś ca naktam ||
english: Let him be far off with body and descendants; let all three earths be below him. O gods, let the glory of him wither who would harm us by day and he who does so by night.

sanskrit: suvijñānaṁ cikituṣe janāya sac cāsac ca vacasī paspṛdhāte | tayo yat satyaṁ yatarat ṛjīyas tad it somo 'vati hanty āsat ||
english: To a person of discernment, the two speeches — truth and untruth — contend. Of these two, whichever is the truth, whichever is the more straight — that Soma protects; he slays the false.

sanskrit: na vā u somo vṛjinaṁ hinoti na kṣatriyam mithuya dhārayantam | hanti rakṣo hanty āsad vadantam ubhāv indrasya prasitau śayāte ||
english: Soma does not advance the crooked man, nor the warrior who holds power falsely. He slays the demon; he slays the speaker of falsehood — both of them lie in the snare of Indra.

sanskrit: yadi vāham anṛtadeva āsa moghaṁ vā devām̐ apyūhe agne | kim asmabhyaṁ jātavedo hṛṇīṣe drogha̱vācas te nirṛthaṁ sacantām ||
english: If I have been a worshipper of false gods, O Agni, or have prayed to the gods in vain — why, O Jātavedas, are you angry with us? Let the treacherous speakers accompany Nirṛti to destruction.

sanskrit: adyā murīya yadi yātudāno asmi yadi vāyus tatapa pūruṣasya | adhā sa vīrair daśabhir vi yūyā yo māṁ moghaṁ yātudānety āha ||
english: May I die today if I am a sorcerer, or if I have scorched any man's life-breath. Let him be torn asunder by ten heroes who calls me falsely a sorcerer.

sanskrit: yo māyātum yātudānety āha yo vā rakṣāḥ śucir asmīty āha | indras taṁ hantu mahatā vadhena viśvasya jantor adhamas padīṣṭa ||
english: He who calls me a sorcerer, a wizard, and he who being an impure demon claims 'I am pure' — let Indra smite him with his great weapon; let him fall to the lowest place of all beings.

sanskrit: pra yā jigāti khargalevā naktam apa druhā tanvaṁ gūhamānā | vavrāṁ anantāṁ ava sā padīṣṭa grāvāṇo ghnantu rakṣasa upadbaiḥ ||
english: She who roams like an owl by night, hiding her body with treachery — let her fall into an endless pit. May the pressing stones strike the demons with their sounds.

sanskrit: vi tiṣṭhadhvam maruto vikṣv icchat gṛbhāyata rakṣasaḥ sam pinaṣṭana | vayo ye bhūtvī patayanti naktabhir ye vā ripo dadhire deve adhvare ||
english: Spread out, O Maruts, searching through the peoples — seize and grind to pieces the demons. Those who have become birds and fly by night, and those who have placed treachery in the divine sacrifice —

sanskrit: pra vartaya divo aśmānam indra somaśitam maghavan saṁ śiśādhi | prāktād apāktād adharād udaktād abhi jahi rakṣasaḥ parvatena ||
english: Hurl down the stone of heaven, O Indra, sharpened by Soma, O bountiful one, sharpen it well. From east, from west, from below, from above — smite the demons with the mountain.

sanskrit: eta u tye patayanti śvayātava indraṁ dipsanti dipsavo 'dābhyam | śiśīte śakraḥ piśunebhyo vadhaṁ nūnaṁ sṛjad aśaniṁ yātumadbhyaḥ ||
english: These — look, they fly about, the dog-wolves, seeking to harm inviolable Indra, the harmers. The Mighty One is sharpening the weapon against the slanderers; now he will let fly his bolt against the sorcerers.

sanskrit: indro yātūnām abhavat parāśaro havirmathīnām abhy āvivāsatām | abhīd u śakraḥ paraśur yathā vanam pātrev bhindan sata eti rakṣasaḥ ||
english: Indra became the destroyer of sorcerers, the supreme one for those who were stealing the oblations as they sought to please. The Mighty One, like an axe splitting a forest, goes forth cleaving to pieces the demons.

sanskrit: ulūkayātuṁ śuśulūkayātuṁ jahi śvayātum uta kokayātum | suparṇayātum uta gṛdhrayātuṁ dṛṣadevā pra mṛṇa rakṣa indra ||
english: Slay the owl-sorcerer, the young-owl-sorcerer, slay the dog-sorcerer, the cuckoo-sorcerer. Slay the eagle-sorcerer, the vulture-sorcerer — O Indra, crush the demons, O stone-crusher.

sanskrit: mā no rakṣo abhi naḍ yātumāvatām apocchat mithunā yā kimīdinā | pṛthivī naḥ pārthivāt pātv aṁhaso 'ntarikṣaṁ divyāt pātv asmān ||
english: Let no demon harm us; let the pair of kimīdins, those who belong to the sorcerers, drive us away. May the earth protect us from earth-dangers; may the atmosphere protect us from heavenly dangers.

sanskrit: indra jahi pumāṁsaṁ yātudānam uta striyam māyayā śāśadānām | vigrīvāso mūradevā ṛdantu mā te dṛśan sūryam uccaṣantam ||
english: O Indra, slay the male sorcerer and also the female who is striking repeatedly with her magic. Let those with bent necks, the foolish-godded ones, be crushed — may they not see the Sun rising.

sanskrit: prati cakṣva vi cakṣvendra ca soma jāgṛtam | rakṣobhyo vadham asyatam aśaniṁ yātumaadbhyaḥ ||
english: Look around, look about — O Indra and Soma, be vigilant. Hurl your weapon at the demons, the thunderbolt at the sorcerers.
